title: Month 32
subtitle: Preschool is a decision this year, and the good places fill early.

baby.development: Your child speaks in sentences of three or more words, can jump, and can pedal a tricycle. They can name a friend and are starting to play with other children rather than beside them.

you.body: If you are pregnant again, the birth plan needs a plan for the older child. Who takes them, where they go, and for how long.
you.mind: Thirty-two months is when the child starts to have a life outside the house. That is the point of preschool, and it is also the thing that makes the first drop-off hard.

coreActions.title: Visit three preschools before you choose
coreActions.why: A preschool is a place your child will spend a thousand hours in, and a brochure cannot tell you what the room feels like.
coreActions.detail: Visit at drop-off, not at tour time. Ask about ratios, staff turnover, how they handle a child who is upset, and what happens when a child bites. Ask what a typical day looks like. Trust the feeling in the room.

coreActions.title: Teach them to write their name, or the first letter
coreActions.why: Writing a name is a three-to-four-year-old skill, and the first letter is where it starts.
coreActions.detail: Write the name in big letters and let the child trace it with a finger, then a crayon. Start with the first letter. Do not correct the grip yet. A child who can recognise their name at three is on track.

coreActions.title: Finish potty learning before preschool starts
coreActions.why: Most preschools expect a child to be out of nappies by three, and the summer before is the easiest time to do it.
coreActions.detail: Pick a week with no travel. Expect accidents. Do not go back to nappies during the day once you start. Night dryness comes later and is not part of it.

alsoKnow.title: The nap may be ending
alsoKnow.body: Most children drop the nap between three and four. A child who is fighting the nap at thirty-two months is more likely overtired than ready to drop it. Quiet time in the afternoon is the bridge.

alsoKnow.title: Twenty teeth, and a check every six months
alsoKnow.body: The full set of baby teeth is complete around three. A dental check every six months from now is the usual schedule.

redFlags.text: Choking — cannot breathe, cough, or make a sound
A fever over 100.4°F with unusual sleepiness or a rash
Feeling hopeless, or thoughts of harming yourself or the child
